methodology.title: 2.1 Core Principle: Dual Component (Math + ELA)
content: Problem: In Phase 2, students must learn both hard academic concepts (Math / Geometry) and the language to explain them (ELA), which can cause cognitive overload if taught simultaneously.

Solution: Every session is strictly split. Part 1 (Math Component, 40 mins) focuses purely on identifying 2D shapes, sides, and corners using detective logic. Part 2 (ELA Component, 80 mins) shifts to the grammatical structures (descriptive adjectives and contrast words like "but") needed to explain the logic step-by-step.

parts.title: PART 1: MATH COMPONENT
content: A. Math Reading Input: The City Clues
Max is a great detective. Today, he is studying geometry (hình học). He looks for a clue (manh mối) in the big city.
Max finds a strange, flat shape on the ground.
"Let's count," says Max. "One, two, three, four. It has exactly four equal sides. It also has four sharp corners."
Max knows the answer! "It is a blue square!"
Then, Max finds another shape. He touches it carefully. "This shape has zero straight sides and zero corners. It goes round and round perfectly. It is a bright red circle!"
→ Memory trick: S-H-A-P-E: See How All Patterns End

content: A. ELA Reading Input: Describing the Clues

"First, I found a flat shape. It has four equal sides. Therefore, it is a beautiful square!"
"Next, I found a shape with no straight lines. It has zero corners. Therefore, it is a perfect circle!"
By using adjectives like 'flat', 'equal', and 'sharp', Max can explain the geometry clues clearly to his friends.

parts.title: PART 1: MATH COMPONENT
content: A. Math Reading Input: Fixing the Broken Bridge
Max and Pip must cross a dangerous river. But the bridge is missing some important pieces!
"We must find the right flat shapes to fix the holes," says Max.
The first hole has zero corners. "We need a perfect circle!" says Pip.
The second hole has four equal sides. "We need a beautiful square!" says Max.
The third hole has three straight sides. "We need a strong green triangle!" says Pip.
By looking at the sides and corners, they find exactly the right shapes to fix the bridge perfectly!

Max writes the rules for the bridge in his notebook.
"First, we observed the holes. We counted the sides and corners carefully. Next, Pip found a circle for the first hole because it goes round and round."
Max looks at the bridge. "Then, I found a square for the second hole. Finally, we used a triangle for the last hole because it is very strong."
They used the three shapes to fix the broken bridge perfectly. Finding shapes and using logic can help you solve many problems!

The diagram shows: A drawing of a house. Arrows point to the roof (Triangle), the main wall (Square), and the door (Rectangle). The math box says: "2D Shapes + Wood = 3D House."

IN-CLASS SPEAKING ACTIVITIES — Session 3 (teacher-led)

Activity 1 — Pair Speaking (3–5 min, pairs):
  Student A: Read the clue: "It has zero sides and zero corners."
  Student B: Tell the logic story: "First, I counted the corners. It has zero. Finally, the shape must be a Circle!"

Challenge Extension (L3 — for advanced / older students):
  L3 — Fill in the blank with 3 options (10 items)
  The circle goes _______________ and round. (round / solve / missing)
  What is the _______________ shape? (missing / logic / rule)
  Max must _______________ the bridge. (fix / repeat / next)
  The next shape _______________ a triangle. (must be / is be / can be)
  The _______________ is very strong. (triangle / next / solve)
  We use _______________ to find the answer. (geometry / repeat / missing)
  First, there _______________ a red circle. (is / are / am)
  The _______________ on the bridge is a square. (shape / logic / solve)
  The _______________ step is to cross the river. (next / repeat / rule)
  The detective solved the _______________. (puzzle / shape / triangle)
